results.name: random_real_range
results.evidence: Global LCG (DAT_00719cd0 = x*0x19660d+0x3c6ef35f) then scales the high 16 bits by 1/65536 and lerps between the two float args, the standard Blam pseudo-random-in-range pattern.
results.summary: Returns a pseudo-random float linearly interpolated between param_1 and param_2 using the engine's global LCG seed.

results.name: vector2d_normalize_with_length
results.evidence: Computes sqrt(x^2+y^2) of the 2-float vector at ECX, and if above the 1e-4 epsilon constant (DAT_00672bd8) divides both components by it in place.
results.summary: Normalizes a 2D vector in place and returns its original length, leaving it unchanged if the length is near zero.

results.name: point3d_add_scaled
results.evidence: out[i] = param_2*dir[i] + base[i] for 3 components (EAX=out, param_1=base, ECX=dir, param_2=scalar): an affine combination / point-along-direction computation.
results.summary: Computes out = base + scale*direction for a 3-component vector (a point offset along a direction by a scalar distance).

results.name: vector3d_length
results.evidence: return sqrt(v.z^2+v.y^2+v.x^2) for the 3-float vector at EAX; no side effects.
results.summary: Returns the Euclidean length of a 3D vector.

results.name: vector3d_normalize_with_length
results.evidence: Computes the length of the 3-vector at ECX, and if it exceeds the ~1e-4 epsilon rescales the vector in place to unit length; otherwise leaves it and returns 0. Mirrors the 2D version at 0x4018e0.
results.summary: Normalizes a 3D vector in place and returns its original length (or 0 if degenerate).

results.name: random_real
results.evidence: Advances the same global LCG seed (DAT_00719cd0) as 0x401050 and returns (seed>>16)*1/65536 with no interpolation, i.e. a value in [0,1).
results.summary: Returns a pseudo-random float in the range [0,1) using the engine's global LCG seed.

results.name: vector3d_distance
results.evidence: sqrt of the sum of squared component differences between the 3-vectors at EAX and ECX -- textbook Euclidean distance.
results.summary: Returns the Euclidean distance between two 3D points.

results.name: sphere_mesh_generate
results.evidence: Copies 6 base vertices from DAT_0065c190 and iterates 8 entries of 3 indices from DAT_0065c1da (6 verts/8 faces = octahedron topology), allocates vertex/index buffers sized by N^2 formulas, and calls FUN_004ca5f0 per face to subdivide it.
results.summary: Builds a subdivided-octahedron point/triangle-index mesh (allocated via GlobalAlloc) used to seed a table of quasi-uniform directions on the unit sphere.

results.name: sphere_mesh_build_face
results.evidence: Allocates a (N+1)^2-sized cache table, walks a triangular grid of barycentric rows for one octahedron face, and calls FUN_004ca7c0 to resolve/cache each subdivided point index while emitting triangle-strip indices.
results.summary: Subdivides one face of the base octahedron into a barycentric grid of points and index triples, caching shared points via a scratch table.

results.name: sphere_mesh_get_face_point
results.evidence: Given barycentric coordinates (param_3,param_4) within a face, returns a cached point index or creates one: falls back to FUN_004ca8c0 for points on a face edge, otherwise allocates a fresh interior index and calls FUN_004ca9a0 to compute it.
results.summary: Resolves (with caching) the point index for a given barycentric position inside a subdivided octahedron face.

results.name: sphere_mesh_get_edge_point
results.evidence: Uses a shared edge-cache array so two adjacent faces reuse the same subdivided points along their common edge, calling FUN_004ca9a0 to fill in unseen edge positions.
results.summary: Resolves (with caching) the shared point index for a position along an edge between two base vertices, so adjacent faces don't duplicate vertices.

results.name: sphere_mesh_interpolate_vertex
results.evidence: Linearly interpolates between two base vertices (param_2,param_3) using fraction in_AX/in_CX, writes the result into the vertex array at param_1, then calls FUN_00401990 to renormalize it back onto the unit sphere -- the classic geodesic-sphere subdivision step.
results.summary: Computes a new sphere-mesh vertex by lerping between two existing vertices and re-projecting the result onto the unit sphere.

results.name: point2d_set_classify
results.evidence: Walks up to param_1 points from an array, calling FUN_0044d950 (an epsilon/sign classifier) and comparing against an accumulated plane, returning a 0/1/2 state; used as the entry test before FUN_004caae0's hull walk.
results.summary: Classifies a point set as degenerate (coincident/collinear) or in general position, feeding the convex-hull builder at 0x4caae0.

results.name: polygon2d_convex_hull_build
results.evidence: After checking degeneracy via FUN_004caa40, finds the lowest point, then repeatedly picks the next hull vertex by minimum polar angle (fpatan) relative to the running direction, writing indices to param_2 until the walk closes back to the start -- a textbook gift-wrapping convex hull.
results.summary: Computes the convex hull of a 2D point array using an angular gift-wrapping walk, returning hull vertex indices.

results.name: polygon2d_point_inside_tolerance
results.evidence: For each polygon edge (Point2D array, ECX), computes the signed perpendicular distance of the test point from the edge line and rejects if it exceeds param_3 outside the edge, matching a tolerant point-in-convex-polygon test.
results.summary: Tests whether a 2D point lies inside a convex polygon within a given distance tolerance.

results.name: polygon2d_point_inside_margin
results.evidence: Same edge-walk structure as 0x4cad80 but compares the raw (un-normalized) edge cross product directly against -param_3 instead of a true perpendicular distance -- a cheaper approximate variant.
results.summary: Cheaper variant of the convex-polygon containment test that compares raw cross-product margin instead of true distance.

results.name: polygon2d_clip_to_planes
results.evidence: Loops param_1 times calling FUN_0044d950 as a trivial-accept test and FUN_004caff0 (single-plane 2D clip) otherwise, double-buffering the vertex list between two 0x400-float stack scratch regions.
results.summary: Iteratively clips a 2D polygon against a sequence of planes/edges, double-buffering the vertex list between clips.

results.name: polygon2d_clip_to_plane
results.evidence: Classic Sutherland-Hodgman clip: walks Point2D vertices (stride 2 floats), tests each against a plane (param_3={a,b,c}), interpolates new vertices at sign changes within tolerance param_7, and merges near-duplicate output points.
results.summary: Clips a 2D polygon against a single line/plane, emitting the clipped vertex list.

results.name: polygon3d_clip_to_plane
results.evidence: Same Sutherland-Hodgman structure as 0x4caff0 but with 3-float stride vertices and a 4-component plane (param_3={a,b,c,d}) -- the 3D counterpart.
results.summary: Clips a 3D polygon against a single plane, emitting the clipped vertex list.

results.name: uint32_log2_floor
results.evidence: Repeatedly right-shifts the ECX argument until it equals 1, counting shifts -- computes the index of the highest set bit (floor(log2(x))).
results.summary: Returns the bit-index of the highest set bit of its (register-passed) integer argument.

results.name: bitvector_or_assign
results.evidence: Computes a word count from a bit count (CX), then ORs 32-bit words from one buffer into another using pointer-offset arithmetic relative to a base (EAX) -- the pattern of a bitset OR/union operation, though register roles could not be fully resolved from the decompilation.
results.summary: Bitwise-ORs one fixed-size bit array into another, word by word.

results.name: matrix4x3_inverse
results.evidence: Pre-existing chimera__ name (hint); code computes the closed-form inverse of the engine's scale+3x3-rotation+translation matrix format (transposes the rotation block, negates/rescales the translation), zeroing the whole matrix when scale is 0.
results.summary: Computes the inverse of a matrix4x3 (uniform scale + rotation + translation).

results.name: matrix4x3_from_axis_angle
results.evidence: Builds a 3x3 rotation block from an axis vector (ECX) and separate sin/cos scalars (param_1,param_2) using exactly the Rodrigues rotation formula (diag = cos+(1-cos)*axis_i^2, off-diag = (1-cos)*axis_i*axis_j +/- sin*axis_k); zeroes the translation.
results.summary: Builds a matrix4x3 rotation from a rotation axis and precomputed sin/cos of the angle (Rodrigues' formula).

results.name: matrix4x3_build_basis_from_vectors
results.evidence: Writes vector ECX into rotation row 0, cross(EAX,ECX) into row 1, and vector EAX into row 2 of a matrix4x3, with scale=1 and translation left untouched -- builds a basis from two input vectors.
results.summary: Builds the rotation part of a matrix4x3 from two vectors and their cross product, leaving scale=1 and translation unset.

results.name: matrix4x3_from_euler_angles
results.evidence: Computes sin/cos of three angle parameters and combines them with the standard 3-axis Euler rotation composition to fill the 3x3 rotation block of a matrix4x3, setting scale=1 and translation=0.
results.summary: Builds a matrix4x3 rotation from three Euler angles.

results.name: matrix4x3_from_quaternion
results.evidence: Uses the standard quaternion-to-rotation-matrix formulas (products of q.x,q.y,q.z,q.w scaled by 2/|q|^2) to fill the 3x3 block of a matrix4x3 at EDX from the quaternion at ECX, zeroing translation.
results.summary: Converts a quaternion (ECX) into the rotation part of a matrix4x3 (EDX).

results.name: quaternion_from_matrix4x3
results.evidence: Classic Shepperd's-method quaternion extraction: checks the trace of the 3x3 block (at offsets +4,+0x14,+0x24, the diagonal of the matrix4x3 rotation), and otherwise picks the largest diagonal element via a cyclic index table (DAT_0069665c).
results.summary: Extracts a quaternion from the rotation part of a matrix4x3.

results.name: matrix4x3_build_from_vectors_and_position
results.evidence: Calls FUN_004cb970 to build the rotation block from two vectors, then copies a 3-float position from an object at unaff_ESI into the translation slots (offsets 0x28/0x2c/0x30, indices 10-12) of the output matrix4x3.
results.summary: Builds a full matrix4x3 (rotation from two vectors, plus a translation copied from another object) in one call.

results.name: matrix4x3_get_basis_and_position
results.evidence: Reads matrix4x3 fields at offsets matching rotation row 0 (+4..+0xc), rotation row 2 (+0x1c..+0x24) and translation (+0x28..+0x30) into three separate output vectors -- the inverse of the fields set by 0x4cbd60/0x4cb970.
results.summary: Unpacks two rotation-basis vectors and the translation out of a matrix4x3 structure.

results.name: matrix4x3_transform_point
results.evidence: Pre-existing chimera__ name (hint); code scales the input point by the matrix's scale field then applies the 3x3 rotation and adds the translation, exactly matrix4x3*point.
results.summary: Transforms a point by a matrix4x3 (scale, rotate, translate).

results.name: matrix4x3_transform_vector
results.evidence: Identical scale+rotate math to matrix4x3_transform_point (0x4cbde0) but omits adding the translation -- transforms a direction/vector rather than a point.
results.summary: Transforms a vector by a matrix4x3's scale and rotation, without translation.

results.name: matrix4x3_transform_normal
results.evidence: Pre-existing chimera__ name (hint); applies only the 3x3 rotation block (no scale, no translation) to the input vector, as appropriate for surface normals.
results.summary: Transforms a normal/direction by only the rotation part of a matrix4x3.

results.name: matrix4x3_transform_plane
results.evidence: Rotates the plane normal (EDX, a Plane3D) by the matrix's 3x3 block the same way transform_vector does, then computes the new distance term as scale*d + dot(new_normal, translation) -- the standard plane-transform formula.
results.summary: Transforms a plane equation (normal+distance) by a matrix4x3.

results.name: matrix4x3_inverse_transform_point
results.evidence: Subtracts the matrix's translation from the input point, divides by scale, then multiplies by the transpose of the 3x3 rotation block -- the closed-form inverse-transform of a point without building a full inverse matrix; zeroes output when scale is 0.
results.summary: Transforms a point from world space into a matrix4x3's local space (inverse transform) without computing a full inverse matrix.

results.name: matrix4x3_inverse_transform_vector
results.evidence: Divides the input vector by the matrix's scale, then multiplies by the transpose of the rotation block (row pattern (1,2,3)/(4,5,6)/(7,8,9), the transpose of transform_vector's column pattern) -- no translation subtracted, matching a vector rather than a point.
results.summary: Transforms a vector from world space into a matrix4x3's local space, without translation.

results.name: matrix4x3_inverse_transform_normal
results.evidence: Multiplies the input vector by the transpose of the 3x3 rotation block only (no scale division, no translation) -- the normal-space counterpart of matrix4x3_inverse_transform_vector.
results.summary: Transforms a normal/direction into a matrix4x3's local space using only the transposed rotation.

results.name: matrix4x3_multiply
results.evidence: Pre-existing chimera__ name (hint); computes param_3 = param_1 * param_2 for the 13-float matrix4x3 layout (scale multiplies together, rotation blocks combine, translation is transformed by param_1), with self-aliasing handled via a local copy.
results.summary: Multiplies two matrix4x3 matrices (param_1 * param_2) into a third.

results.name: matrix4x3_multiply_sse
results.evidence: Same input/output layout and self-aliasing handling as matrix4x3_multiply (0x4cc0d0) but implemented with PackedFloatingMUL/ADD (SSE packed-float) intrinsics; installed as the multiply function pointer at 0x4cd3f0 when a CPU feature test (bit 0x1a) passes.
results.summary: SSE-optimized implementation of matrix4x3 multiplication, selected at startup when the CPU supports the required feature.

results.name: matrix3x3_transpose
results.evidence: Swaps the three off-diagonal pairs of a 9-float matrix (indices 1<->3, 2<->6, 5<->7) in place when source==dest, or writes the full transpose to a separate destination otherwise.
results.summary: Transposes a 3x3 matrix, handling in-place (aliased) transposition.

results.name: matrix3x3_build_basis_from_vectors
results.evidence: Writes vector EDX into row 0, cross(ECX,EDX) into row 1, and vector ECX into row 2 of a 9-float output -- the pure-Matrix (no scale/translate) counterpart of 0x4cb970.
results.summary: Builds a 3x3 basis matrix from two vectors and their cross product.

results.name: matrix3x3_multiply
results.evidence: Standard 3x3*3x3 matrix multiply formula over two 9-float inputs, with self-aliasing handled by copying to a local 9-float buffer first; matches the tags.h Matrix (float m[3][3]) layout.
results.summary: Multiplies two 3x3 matrices.

results.name: matrix3x3_inverse_transform_vector
results.evidence: Multiplies the input vector by the matrix using column-stride access (0,3,6 / 1,4,7 / 2,5,8), the transpose of a normal row-multiply, with self-aliasing handled via local copy -- matches the transpose/inverse pattern used elsewhere for orthonormal matrices.
results.summary: Transforms a vector by the transpose of a 3x3 matrix (inverse transform for an orthonormal matrix).

results.name: quaternion_from_matrix3x3
results.evidence: Same Shepperd's-method structure as quaternion_from_matrix4x3 (0x4cbc00) but reading the diagonal at plain 3x3 offsets (0,4,8) and using a separate cyclic-index table (DAT_00696668) sized for a 9-float matrix.
results.summary: Extracts a quaternion from a 3x3 rotation matrix.

results.name: periodic_function_tables_init
results.evidence: Allocates twelve 0x400-byte buffers (DAT_006b7aa8 array) filled via FUN_004ccdb0 and six more (DAT_006b7ad8) filled via FUN_004cccb0, matching the lookup tables consumed by periodic_function_evaluate's DAT_006b7aa8 indexing.
results.summary: Allocates and fills the byte lookup tables backing the engine's periodic (wave) function evaluator.

results.name: periodic_function_tables_free
results.evidence: Frees the same eighteen buffers (DAT_006b7aa8[12] and DAT_006b7ad8[6]) allocated by 0x4cc8d0, guarded by the DAT_006b7af0 init flag.
results.summary: Frees the periodic-function lookup tables allocated by periodic_function_tables_init.

results.name: periodic_function_evaluate
results.evidence: Pre-existing chimera__ name (hint); samples one of the DAT_006b7aa8 byte tables at a phase derived from param_1 (time) via FUN_00628cca, interpolating between adjacent samples and handling wraparound for certain function types.
results.summary: Samples the precomputed periodic (wave) function table selected by the type index in AX at the given time, returning an interpolated [0,1] value.

results.name: periodic_function_evaluate_at_phase
results.evidence: Clamps param_1 to [0,1] and uses it directly as a table phase (rather than deriving phase from time as 0x4cc9b0 does), indexing the secondary DAT_006b7ad8 table set by in_CX.
results.summary: Samples one of the secondary periodic-function tables at an explicit [0,1] phase rather than by elapsed time.

results.name: periodic_function_build_warp_table
results.evidence: Fills a 1024-float array with a running sum of (1 + weighted cosines at three frequencies + jittered LCG noise), then normalizes the whole array by the final accumulated total -- produces a monotonically increasing warp curve used by 0x4ccdb0's 'variant' cosine case.
results.summary: Builds a normalized cumulative noise/warp table used to distort one of the periodic wave types.

results.name: periodic_function_build_variant_table
results.evidence: Fills a 1024-byte table using a switch on an outer selector, calling an external noise routine (FUN_006283c0) for most cases and a raw sine for the last, then quantizing each sample to a byte via FUN_006391b4 -- the secondary-table counterpart of FUN_004ccdb0.
results.summary: Builds one of the six secondary periodic-function byte tables.

results.name: periodic_function_build_table
results.evidence: Switches on a type index 0-11 to fill a 1024-sample float buffer (constant 1/0, cosine, cosine warped via 0x4ccbb0's table, folded/raw noise from FUN_00628cca, per-sample LCG noise, and sums of sines/cosines), tracks min/max, then quantizes to bytes via FUN_006391b4 into the output table.
results.summary: Builds one of the twelve primary periodic-function byte lookup tables (constant, cosine, noise, wander, etc.) for a given type index.

results.name: random_seed_generate
results.evidence: Combines the CRT rand() with two QueryPerformanceCounter readings converted to milliseconds via 64-bit division, XOR-ing all three together.
results.summary: Produces a hard-to-predict seed value by XOR-combining rand() with two high-resolution timer readings.

results.name: sphere_point_table_init
results.evidence: Seeds a second global RNG state (DAT_00719cd4) from random_seed_generate, builds a sphere mesh via FUN_004ca4b0, and copies its vertex array into the global DAT_006b7af4/DAT_006b7af8 point table before freeing the mesh's scratch buffers.
results.summary: Initializes the global table of quasi-uniform unit-sphere sample points used for randomized directions.

results.name: random_real_range_seeded
results.evidence: Same LCG-and-lerp formula as random_real_range (0x401050), but advances an explicit seed pointed to by ECX rather than the global DAT_00719cd0 -- a per-object/instance random generator.
results.summary: Returns a pseudo-random float between two bounds, advancing a caller-supplied RNG state instead of the global seed.

results.name: random_scatter_direction
results.evidence: Copies a 3-float point from EAX, advances the DAT_00719cd4 seed, normalizes it via FUN_00401990, and (if non-degenerate) picks a random angle in [param_1,param_2] to compute sin/cos which it passes to FUN_004cd820 -- consistent with generating a randomized dispersion direction, though several register roles couldn't be pinned down from this fragment alone.
results.summary: Helper that derives a randomly rotated direction (used for weapon/effect dispersion) from a sphere sample point and a random angle.

results.name: vector2d_normalize
results.evidence: Normalizes the 2-float vector at ECX in place if its squared length is non-zero; unlike 0x4018e0 it uses a plain !=0 check and does not return the original length.
results.summary: Normalizes a 2D vector in place (no length returned, no epsilon tolerance).

results.name: vector3d_normalize
results.evidence: Same pattern as 0x4cd2e0 but for a 3-float vector at ECX.
results.summary: Normalizes a 3D vector in place (no length returned, no epsilon tolerance).

results.name: vector3d_cross_product_length
results.evidence: Computes the full 3-component cross product of the vectors at EAX and ECX, then returns SQRT of the sum of its squared components -- i.e. only the magnitude of the cross product is returned, not the vector.
results.summary: Returns the magnitude of the cross product of two 3D vectors (e.g. twice the area of the triangle they span).

results.name: math_initialize
results.evidence: Calls sphere_point_table_init and periodic_function_tables_init, installs matrix4x3_multiply as the default multiply function pointer then upgrades it to SSE/3DNow variants based on CPU-feature checks (FUN_005402a0), and scans the command line for the "-noSSE" string to skip that upgrade.
results.summary: One-time engine startup routine that initializes the math subsystem's tables and selects the best available matrix-multiply implementation for the CPU.

results.name: vector2d_angle_between
results.evidence: Computes acos of the clamped dot product of two 2D vectors (unaff_ESI, unaff_EDI) via FUN_00628140, then negates the result if their cross product (z) is negative -- a signed angle-between-vectors.
results.summary: Returns the signed angle between two 2D vectors.

results.name: vector3d_angle_between
results.evidence: Computes the angle between two 3D vectors (ECX,EDX) using the cos(2*theta)=2*cos^2(theta)-1 identity on the normalized dot product before calling acos (FUN_00628140) and halving, with a supplementary-angle correction when the dot product is negative -- a precision-friendly way to get the unsigned angle between vectors.
results.summary: Returns the unsigned angle between two 3D vectors.
